# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

Allow a longer notepad, or a separate structured log field for per-night results. Mark clearly in the event log which messages were private, and to whom, without requiring the reader to infer it from the ledger.

answers.confusing_rules: R22 budget: the trial-only budget and the 'accused's first defense free up to 150 words' interact unclearly with the per-message price formula, and I could not tell whether the 1x trial price stacks with the multiplier. R1/R1-style win checks after night deaths with Executioner and Jester revenge were hard to sequence: revenge Divine Attacks land the night after a Day, but the Night 2 deaths of Erin and Mallory were only shown at Day 3 start. Also unclear whether a Scout result given on Night 1 counts as 'known' before the next Day. Oracle guesses are Astral, so it is unclear whether a correct Oracle guess is verifiable by anyone other than the claimant.
answers.missing_information: I could not see the speaking budget or the price table in this summary, so I could not judge how much I could afford to say. Night chat of the Yakuza was not visible to me and I could not tell whether teammates were reporting the same Katana holder as the moderator. I had no record of the role census (how many Yakuza, Neutrals, Roleplayers exist), so I could not tell whether a role claim was possible. Token counts for claimed roles (Oracle, Diviner, Scout) were not shown, which made claim checks guesswork.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to see my own private messages and any night-chat outcomes when I was alive, plus a clear list of who had revenge-killed whom and why, to check claims before voting. I wanted to post a short concrete Night 1 read to Heidi and Ivan privately, but the moderator's log only shows PMs as sender-recipient counts, so I could not confirm delivery or contents. I also could not update my last will on a Day after death, and I had no simple way to compare my notepad with the public ledger line by line.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Mallory and Erin died on Night 2 (revenge kills) but their deaths only appeared as Day 3 announcements, with no night-time notice to them; the timeline shows the Day 2 night summary to Alice as the only Night 2 death notice. Alice's Night 1 Scout result was delivered privately on Night 1 yet she claimed on Day 1 that she had no results, which looks like a timing inconsistency in the claim record. Frank's Day 4 last will stated votes that differ slightly from the posted trial record (Yes on Bob's nomination was listed as a vote for Grace's failed nomination). The Day 2 nomination of Judy lists 'Dave' among Yes votes while Dave is also the Executioner, which is consistent but worth a note. Fortune Teller numbers 2 and 2 were repeated each night, which the program never explained.
answers.suggestions: Include the speaking budget and price table in every summary and in the public ledger so players can plan. Announce revenge kills and their cause to the affected player at night, not only at the next Day start. Show the number of Yakuza alive and the role census count (without names) once a role is revealed as Yakuza-only. Keep a clearer per-night public log of who was attacked and whether the attack succeeded. Allow dead players to submit a final short message after death so their last will can add a corrected read. Show private messages' contents to the recipient in the next turn prompt so players do not have to reconstruct them.

answers.confusing_rules: The Diviner's group rule (the target plus nearest neighbours, skipping yourself, with the exact role drawn from one member at 60/20/20) and the Oracle's and Cartographer's visit-group wording were hard to apply without repeated re-reading. Swap and Katana interactions also need careful reading. The line that a Katana attack counts as the holder's visit, while passing it does not, was easy to misapply when reasoning about who visited whom.
answers.missing_information: I could not see the actual visit log on any night, only the Lookout claim and the Fortune Teller's two numbers, so visit-based checks depended on single claims. The speaking budget and remaining budget per turn were hard to track across Days, and I could not see how much budget other players had left, which affects how much they can say in a trial. It was also unclear how many trials remained that Day, and whether the Day 3 nomination limit counted failed nominations.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to ask one player (Carol) a direct private question about her Oracle guesses without it being visible as a private message to everyone, since private messages are announced to the whole table. I also wanted to see a full, consistent record of every nomination and vote total in one place, including the speaking budget spent, to judge how much each player could say before a trial.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Several things felt inconsistent. Judy's Day 1 self-nomination was recorded as a Yes from Judy and Dave, but the vote text listed Judy's own Yes as the nominator default, which is correct, yet the phrasing made it hard to tell. The death announcements of Erin and Mallory came as Day 3 announcements of Night 2 revenge deaths, while the ledger lists them as Night 2 deaths, which made timing confusing. Carol's public Oracle claim was posted with an N3 guess result only on Day 4 even though the result was known at Night 3, which is by design but felt odd.
answers.suggestions: Show a short running status each turn: living players, nominations left that Day, trials left, and each player's remaining budget. Label private messages with a clearer reminder that their existence is public. Include a brief per-night visit summary for Lookout-style roles in the moderator log so claims can be checked against a single source. Consider a short glossary of exact-role and alignment check terms in the prompt, since those are referenced constantly.

answers.confusing_rules: The Diviner group rule (nearest neighbour on each side, skipping yourself, never counting anyone twice, among players alive at the start of the night) was hard to apply once players had died, because dead players leave the circle and I had to rebuild the neighbours by hand each night. The speaking budget rule (2.5 per round up to 8, 50% carry-over, price = (1 + words/60 + (words/200)^2) x round multiplier, PMs at 0.25x, trial budget of 2) was clear in principle but hard to use without a running balance. It was also unclear whether the accused's free 150-word defence counts against the 800-word cap.
answers.missing_information: A full visit log for the whole village each night (who visited whom), so that claims such as the Lookout's or the Scout's could be checked against actual visits rather than only the claimant's own result. My current speaking-budget balance and the price table for each turn, which I was told would appear in each turn prompt but which I could not see in the summary. A seat-numbered list of players alive at the start of each night, to compute Diviner or Scout groups without error.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to see the price table and my remaining budget when deciding how long to speak, and I could not. I wanted to correct an earlier public statement after new information came in, and there was no way to amend a message once posted. Day coordination with teammates had to happen in public or in short private messages that everyone could see the existence of, so I could not plan a Day-time move without signalling it.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing I could confirm as broken. The Fortune Teller numbers matched the visits each night (2 and 2 on Nights 1 and 2), which is consistent with the rules. The revenge deaths of Erin and Mallory on Night 2 were announced under Day 3, which made the timing easy to misread. The Scout's Night 2 result (Bob, Erin and Heidi in separate groups) was consistent with the visits but very hard to check by hand because the groups are built from visit links in both directions.
answers.suggestions: Publish a per-night visit list (visitor to visited) or at least the visit groups, so that any claim can be checked by everyone. Show the speaking budget and price table in every turn prompt, including the remaining balance. Whenever a random-group role reports, include the living-at-night-start roster with seat numbers. For revenge kills, state the night the death happened and the trial it came from, so the timing is unambiguous.

answers.confusing_rules: The Clerk's rig timing was hard to pin down: the rig is set at night for the next Day, but the prompts never made clear whether a rigged nomination still needs a trial vote to pass, or whether the rig is announced when it fails. The Katana rules are also dense. The holder appears Good, the holder may use their own role on the same night, and passing the Katana is not a visit, so it took careful reading to know which night's holder mattered. The R19 exceptions for Neutrals, framed players and the Ex-Con were easy to misapply, and the Census Taker exception was not obvious.
answers.missing_information: I had no running view of my own speaking budget or the price table in the final summary, so I could not tell how much I could still say on Day 4. I also could not see the timing of every night action, such as whether a teammate's Clerk or Fabricator use would be submitted before or after the Katana vote. The public ledger did not show which claims had been checked against which results, which made it hard to track whether a Lookout or Oracle claim had been contradicted.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to spend my Clerk token on a rigged Day, but I never got a clean chance to test whether a non-teammate nominee would be picked, so I had to hold it. I also wanted a private way to coordinate with teammates on a daytime vote without the PM itself being visible to everyone; the rules make every PM's existence public, which made any teammate contact a visible signal. I could not check a claimed role's contents without the claimant's cooperation.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Night 1 Scout result for Alice said Dave, Erin and Grace were each in a different visit group, but Erin was then killed by a Jester revenge and Mallory by an Executioner revenge on the same cycle, which made the death timing hard to line up with the trial votes. Bob's Lookout result for Night 3 reported that nobody visited Grace while the Katana holder had attacked Bob, which is consistent with the rules, but it meant the Lookout could not see the Katana visit that a Tracker would have seen. The Day 3 ledger also grouped the Night 2 visit summary for Alice as Bob, Erin and Heidi, which is a visit-group result rather than a visit list, and that wording is easy to misread.
answers.suggestions: Show each player's remaining speaking budget and the current price table in the final summary, not only at the start of each turn. Make the Clerk's rig outcome explicit in the ledger (announced or not, and whether it passed). Put a short note in the public ledger when a claim has been checked against a moderator result, so players do not have to reconstruct that. Consider a single line in the rules text stating what the Katana holder's visit shows to a Lookout, since that was the main point of dispute on Day 3. The notepad 375-word cap was fine, though a per-player line format would help more if the cap were larger.

answers.confusing_rules: The Fabricator's frame and the Yakuza Katana rules were hard to hold together: the frame makes a player look Evil to alignment checks, but nothing says whether that also changes how a Lookout or Tracker reads the visit. Revenge timing was also unclear: the Executioner's and Jester's revenge kills happen the night after the hang, but the Day announcements presented them as Day deaths, so the timeline needed a second read. The speaking budget and trial-only budget rules were stated, but I never saw my actual budget or price table in this transcript, so I could not check how much I could say.
answers.missing_information: I could not see my own speaking budget, the price table, or how much budget the other players had left. I also had no clear per-night record of tokens remaining for each Yakuza, only what I had written in my notepad. The Fortune Teller numbers and Diviner groups were useful but hard to cross-check without a running list of who visited whom each night, so I kept reconstructing that by hand.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to submit a Fabricator frame on Carol or Frank for a later Sheriff-style read, but the night interface only let me record Katana votes and no role action, so I could not tell whether a frame target could be entered. I also wanted to learn whether a teammate's night action could be seen in full before the night closed, so I could coordinate a frame and a Katana target together.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The death announcements put Erin and Mallory under Day 3 even though the ledger lists them as Night 2 deaths from the Jester and Executioner revenge. The Day 3 reveal did not state the night they died, which made the order of events hard to follow. Judy's Day 1 self-nomination was recorded as a failed nomination with 3 Yes, which is consistent with the rules, but the will text called it a deliberate test, so public and private records of the same event read differently. The Scout result given to Alice (Dave, Erin and Grace in separate groups) was also reported to me as the same result she posted, which is correct but made it impossible to verify her claim from my side.
answers.suggestions: Show each living player's remaining budget and tokens in the turn prompt, and show the price table each turn in the same place. Add a night-action entry for role actions such as a Fabricator frame so the target can be recorded explicitly. Label revenge deaths with the night they occurred, not the Day they were announced. Keep a short public ledger of visits per night for Lookouts and Trackers so players can cross-check claims without rebuilding the record by hand.

answers.confusing_rules: The Jester and Executioner revenge rules were hard to track: a revenge fires on the night after the Day of the hanging, but the death is announced later, so the timing is easy to misread. The Diviner and Seer group rules (nearest neighbours, skipping self, players who die that night can be drawn) were also hard to apply without a seating diagram. R23 swap wording about how results are named was dense. The Roleplayer and Ex-Con alignment exceptions needed careful rereading.
answers.missing_information: I could not see a running record of each player's speaking budget, so I could not judge who could afford a long trial defence. The public ledger does not list visit groups or which players were in them, so checking Scout, Diviner or Oracle groups meant reconstructing the circle by hand. A per-player status line (alive, role if revealed, budget left, votes cast this Day) would have helped.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As Jester I wanted a clear way to say 'I am the Jester' without that being read as a claim I cannot back up, and a way to show that my self-nomination was a test without making it look like a steering attempt. I also wanted to see the other players' private night-chat summaries in aggregate form, which I could not, since I was not in Yakuza chat. Speaking budget was hard to plan around because the price table shows only the current turn.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broken. Mildly odd: Oracle and Lookout results were posted with a Day delay while the Ritualist-style announcement rules are different, which makes the timing of public information uneven. The Day 3 public message from Bob asserting 'the moderator said' was not a public fact, so it read as a claim, not a result. The Judy trial vote total of 10 Guilty from 11 votes was announced correctly, but nobody could verify individual PMs, which made the 'vote test' accusation impossible to disprove.
answers.suggestions: Show a short per-turn status block with alive players, deaths with revealed roles, and each player's remaining budget. Add a visit-group summary for Scout and Diviner results, or at least the seating circle at the start of each night. Clarify in the rules that a Jester's revenge targets are chosen from the trial's Guilty voters alive at the start of the following night, with an example. Allow a longer notepad, since 375 words is tight for a game of this length.

answers.confusing_rules: The Fortune Teller's two numbers are hard to use: when a visit pattern could produce the same pair in several ways, I couldn't tell which number was visited and which was visitors, so the result was nearly useless. The Katana rule (holder visits, passing is not a visit, holder appears Good) and the Oracle's Astral Visit with a 'correct/wrong' result were also easy to misread under time pressure. The speaking-budget price formula (1 + words/60 + (words/200)^2, times the round multiplier, with trial-only budget) was hard to plan around without a worked example.
answers.missing_information: I could not see a running count of how many Yakuza were alive, or whether the Katana holder had changed, without reconstructing it from public deaths and announcements. The Day-start death announcements can list deaths from the previous night, so I had to work out timing myself. I also lacked a compact per-player table of claims, votes and PMs; the public ledger helped, but I had to keep my own notepad current. Speaking-budget balances for the other players were not visible, which mattered for judging who could still push a trial.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to ask the moderator a yes/no question about how a specific visit result would have looked under the swap or Katana rules, but there was no clarification channel. I wanted to privately share my Fortune Teller numbers with one trusted player without sending a PM whose existence everyone sees; the private message system made every PM public in its existence, which I had to account for. I also wanted to see the full list of private message contents for players I suspected, which only Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps can do, so I could not test a PM-based theory directly.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Day 3 log lists Alice, Erin and Mallory as dying on Day 3 while the ledger lists them as Night 2 deaths; this is probably announcement timing but it reads as an inconsistency. The Fortune Teller result was reported as '2 and 2' on both nights, which made it hard to tell whether this was coincidence or a sign that numbers were sometimes padded. The Diviner's 'which is which isn't given' note appeared on some results but not others, so the disclosure rule looks inconsistent. Some Day 1 and Day 2 summaries were repeated across the public and private logs, making the transcript long to scan.
answers.suggestions: Add a short per-day public state line (alive players, Yakuza count, current Katana holder if publicly known) so players do not have to reconstruct it. Give Fortune Teller numbers with a clearer convention, or report the visited and visitor counts separately, or say explicitly that they are ambiguous. Provide a worked speaking-budget example in the prompt, including what a 60-word public message costs at round 1 and round 5. Allow a single short factual question to the moderator each Day, answered only to the asker, so rule ambiguities can be resolved in play. Deduplicate repeated summaries in the end-of-game transcript.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Results for players who die that night. The Scout (Alice, killed N2) and Fortune Teller (Mallory, killed by Executioner revenge N2) both still produced Night 2 output. R10 says end-of-night investigations report on everyone alive when the night began. It does not say whether a player who dies that night still receives their own result. This matters most for the Fortune Teller, whose numbers come 'at the start of each Day', when Mallory was already dead. I delivered both results, but I could have gone either way. 2) The Executioner 'leaves' rather than dies. R13 shares a last will 'when a player dies', and leaving 'works exactly like dying' except for death counts. I revealed Dave's will, but the rules don't say whether a will belongs to that reveal. 3) A Jester hanging and an Executioner win on the same trial create two Divine revenge draws the same night from the same Guilty-voter pool. The rules don't say whether the draws are independent (could they hit the same player?) or ordered. I drew them independently, and they hit Erin and Mallory. 4) The Diviner/Surveyor group 'among players alive at the start of the night'. Dave had left the circle on Day 2, so Carol's N2 group skipped him (Bob, Carol, Erin). The rule only implies this through R11. 5) The Fortune Teller 'Day' timing versus results being computed at night end: the log shows them under the night.
answers.missing_information: I had no built-in visit graph. To check Mallory's FT numbers (2/2 both nights), Alice's Scout groups and Bob's Lookout results, I rebuilt visits by hand. I had to remember that Oracle guesses and both revenge attacks are Astral and add no visits, and that the Katana adds Grace->Alice on N2 on top of her Diviner visit to Carol. A live circle view showing removed seats would have helped with Diviner neighbors (the skip-self rule changed Frank's N3 group to Carol, Frank, Heidi). A list of Guilty voters still eligible for revenge, excluding the dead Judy and the departed Dave, would also have helped.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to attach a short note to a result such as 'you died tonight; this is your final result'. I also wanted to send Grace a single Yakuza summary that matched the one her teammates got, instead of a separate version. Neither was supported cleanly.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) The Yakuza summaries were inconsistent across nights. N1 sent Grace a different summary that left out her own action, while N2-N4 sent one shared summary to all three. 2) The N4 summary says Heidi 'did not use her Clerk action'. Clerk is a token-only, optional action, so the wording suggests something was skipped. 3) Results were delivered to players who died that night (Alice's N2 Scout names, Mallory's N2 FT numbers). The FT numbers in particular are a Day-start result going to a player who was dead by that Day. 4) Bob's N3 Lookout result and death notice were merged into one message. That is fine, but inconsistent with the other nights. Otherwise I checked the mechanics and they were correct: FT 2/2 both nights, all Scout groups, Lookout results, every Diviner group, both revenge draws from valid Guilty voters, nomination thresholds, and the final win (Yakuza plus Jester and Executioner).
answers.suggestions: Add a moderator visit-graph and circle-state panel that automatically computes FT numbers, Scout and Cartographer groups, and neighbor groups. State explicitly in R10 whether a player who dies at night still gets that night's own results, and whether the Fortune Teller gets numbers if dead by Day start. In R13 and the Executioner text, state whether a departing Executioner's will is revealed. Specify that simultaneous Jester and Executioner revenges draw independently, and say what happens if both pick the same player. Use one standard Yakuza summary template, identical for every member, that lists every member's chosen action including the recipient's own. Consider a parity or lock-win rule, since N3-N4 played out a foregone Yakuza majority.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: A single watch that names one visitor is only as good as the visit model; before accusing, check whether the kill could have come from a different holder or a self-visit, and ask for a second watch or a Veteran-style confirmation instead of pushing a trial on one log.
Private whips for a Yes vote on a single unverified claim are visible as a pattern (the PM counts are public); if you need votes, make the case in public with the evidence so the table can check it.

Track which claimed roles are Yakuza-only (Diviner, Ritualist, Clerk, Fabricator): a player who publicly claims one of them is a strong Yakuza lead, and reading that claim against kill timing and nominations beats weighing wording.

Yakuza who keep a passive partner (no action, no PMs) let the Village vote on the other members' speeches; rotate visible activity and keep nominations aligned with the Village's own suspicions to avoid being the only one who pushes.

Post your full night log in your first speech after getting it, and state explicitly which parts depend on a single claim; a Lookout who names only the target and its visitor leaves no test for a denial.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting.
tips_feedback.why: Stating my Grace lean and then voting Yes on her only after the Lookout log kept the table's read on my vote clear.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: The Grace denial versus the Lookout log was a concrete contradiction I could point at, which kept my Yes vote grounded.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: I kept my watch target private, and Yakuza still had to infer it from the public Lookout claim rather than from my statements.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily.
tips_feedback.why: The Oracle and Diviner group data let us cross-check Carol and Grace's claims against counts, which is what exposed Grace's Diviner claim.

tips_feedback.tip: Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans.
tips_feedback.why: My will carried my Night 1 to 3 results and the Night 3 plan, so my visit data survived my death for the Village.

output.reason: Answering the post-game reflection with concrete reusable lessons and the tips that clearly mattered.

Carol: claims Oracle (N1 Judy Jester correct, N2 Alice Scout correct); voted Yes on Grace to force an answer; likely Good, check N3 guess. Frank: privately whipped Heidi and Ivan for Yes on Grace on one claim; voted Yes; suspicious, watch. Heidi: No on Grace until second source; fair so far. Ivan: No on Grace; asks for checkable reads; fair so far. Plan: Night 3 watch Grace (keep private). No nomination until Night 3 result is out.
notepad_after: Grace: sole visitor of Alice N2 per my Lookout, so Katana holder and Yakuza; denies visit, claims Diviner (Yakuza-only). Strong lean Yakuza. Carol: claims Oracle (N1 Judy Jester correct, N2 Alice Scout correct); voted Yes on Grace to force an answer; likely Good, check N3 guess. Frank: privately whipped Heidi and Ivan for Yes on Grace on one claim; voted Yes; suspicious, watch. Heidi: No on Grace until second source; fair so far. Ivan: No on Grace; asks for checkable reads; fair so far. Plan: Night 3 watch Grace (keep private). No nomination until Night 3 result is out.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Before trusting a single Lookout or Tracker watch, check whether the death it explains is consistent with the Katana rule (holder must visit target) and with any other visit data; a lone watch naming one player is strong but must be cross-checked against a second source before a hang.
Do not whip private votes on one unverified claim; when a player pushes Yes/Guilty by PM before any second source exists, that pattern is itself a suspicious tell that the village can punish.

When a claimed Oracle's guesses are verified by public deaths and reveals, treat their remaining guess targets as high-value; a Yakuza who is about to be exposed will kill the verified Oracle quickly, so protect or reveal the Oracle's results early.

Track the Yakuza's Katana holder across nights from the Katana-hit deaths: if the same player is always the one whose vote and visits line up, a Diviner claim by that player is a confirmed Yakuza signal and the village should vote on it immediately.
When a claimed Diviner or other Yakuza-only role is publicly named, a Village player who claims it is almost certainly lying; treat such claims as a Yakuza signal rather than a neutral read.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Forced concrete reasoning in the Judy trial (self-nomination vote, PM test, threatened Guilty on Alice) and kept hanging decisions tied to recorded facts rather than vibes.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's Lookout watch on Alice named Grace, which was the only real visit evidence; reasoning from the visit alone (not the action) was the key to the Grace nomination.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them.
tips_feedback.why: Yakuza kept night chat only and used no daytime PMs, while the village-side Judy and Dave PM trail became a public case that drew the whole town into a hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's public Oracle guesses were predictable targets and Carol was killed by the Katana the next night, consistent with the warning.

output.reason: Reflecting on the completed game to give reusable lessons and feedback on the tips that mattered.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Oracle guesses are Astral Visits that reveal only correct/incorrect; a guess on a role that a living Yakuza is publicly tied to (e.g. Diviner) confirms that player's alignment, so pick guesses that split the suspect pool rather than repeating the same confirmed role claim.

Do not publicly post a wrong or unverifiable guess target as a plan; the Yakuza read the Oracle's Night 4 target as the real Oracle and killed her, so an Oracle who announces guesses early is a Katana target from the next night.

A single unverified claim (Scout, Lookout) plus a private whip for votes is weaker than it looks; demand a second independent source before voting, and treat coordinated PMs asking for a Yes as a visible pattern to flag early.

If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: A Katana attack is a visit by its holder, so a living Lookout or Tracker who watched the target that night names the holder. Before committing to a kill, check whether a Good watcher might be on the target, and kill or move the Katana away from a holder whose visit trail is already public.

Never post Yakuza-only results (a Diviner group, Katana or Clerk actions) in daytime chat. Grace's public Diviner results became proof of Yakuza membership once Carol's Oracle guess confirmed the role.

Do not flatly deny a visit that a Lookout could have seen. Grace's denial of the Night 2 visit to Alice was contradicted by Bob's watch, and that contradiction carried the Village's vote. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit it, or stay vague.

A one-shot token held to the end is wasted. My Clerk token went unused and was lost when the game ended with me alive. Use a rig on a Day when a non-teammate nominee would pass, or before the Yakuza's influence on the vote is lost.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action... A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's Lookout log named Grace as Alice's only visitor, and with Alice dead to the Katana it was close to proof. It drove the Day 3 nomination and Frank's pressure on the vote, and I could not counter it without the Katana log being visible.

tips_feedback.why: The three of us matched holder and target every night, so the Katana kills on Alice, Bob and Carol all landed.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted.
tips_feedback.why: The advice was right. I held my Clerk token instead of spending it on a decisive Day, and it was lost when the game ended.

lessons.tip: A Katana kill needs its holder's visit, so a Lookout watch showing a lone visitor on the victim is a checkable contradiction against a bare denial. Ask the denier for the one fact that would disprove the moderator-confirmed log, and weigh it above speeches.

Do not whip votes by private message on one unverified claim. Every PM is visible to all, so it shows who pushed, and Yakuza can frame the whipper, as happened to Frank on Day 4. Post the argument publicly and let votes follow.

A self-nomination followed by pushing a hang and arguing for the rope is a Jester tell. If the Village is unsure, prefer waiting over a lethal vote, because a Jester hang wins for them and their revenge kills a random Guilty voter, as with Erin and Mallory.

Once a correct Oracle guess identifies a Yakuza-only role, the Yakuza will target you next night, as Carol was on Night 4. Post the result promptly and pair it with a living ally who can vouch for you, so the Village has a second source if you die.

tips_feedback.tip: A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor.

Never publicly post results from a Yakuza-only role such as Diviner or Ritualist. Posting them confirms your alignment to everyone, so claim a role that is compatible with a Village player or stay silent.
Keep the Katana on the holder with the least exposure and move it when a visible watcher names the holder. A holder who is also the one Village players can point to is the easiest target.
Spend a one-shot token (Clerk rig) on a decisive Day while a non-teammate can be nominated. An unused token at the end of the game is wasted, and a failed nomination can cost the whole Day.

Kill or neutralise that watcher before its next watch, or move the Katana the same night. We kept Grace as holder for four nights, and Bob's single watch on Alice exposed her.

Village players who privately push a vote on one claim become easy hang targets. When a teammate is accused of this in public, nominate the accuser or the whipper at once, as Grace did with Frank, rather than defending a teammate with a single-claim argument.

Keep your trial speech about checkable facts on other players; begging for a Guilty vote or saying you would rather hang is what got the Village to convict me by 10 to 1.

When a Village group hangs one suspect, it has to stay on the same contradiction: once Frank and the Village argued from Bob's single Lookout log, the Yakuza simply nominated Frank and the Village split, so only hang on evidence that outlives the claimant.

Count the living Village claims before picking a Katana target; the Yakuza killed the real Oracle the night after she guessed Grace's Diviner role correctly, so an Oracle who is still alive after a correct guess on a Yakuza is the first kill to make.

Check whether a Katana attack actually happened by its visit trail: a Lookout's single visitor on a victim is strong evidence, but the Diviner's own group shows only who was near the target, so do not treat group membership as a visit.

tips_feedback.why: I relied on the Dave-to-Judy PM and the Bob-to-Judy PMs as the lead, and the Village used exactly that trail to hang me, even though a Jester also leaves PM trails.

lessons.tip: Fortune Teller numbers (for example 2 and 2) are only a consistency check: they count visited players and visitors without saying which is which. Use them to reject claims that imply more visits than the numbers allow, not to confirm a single named visit.

Publicly revealing or claiming a Yakuza-only role such as Diviner, or posting Yakuza-chat-style group results, is a near-certain tell. If you must reveal, do it only when a Good claimant would make the same claim, and never invent a result that a Village role could contradict.

A player who self-nominates, votes Yes for themselves, and then argues for their own trial may be a Jester who wins by hanging. Before voting Guilty on that pattern, check whether the hang gives them a win, and weigh that more than the contradictions they are accused of.

Investigators who learn a true result should write it into their will, labelled as results. Bob's will carried his real Lookout watches after death and was the only visit evidence the Village could still use.

summary: The Village lost by giving away its numbers on Day 2. Judy (Jester) self-nominated on Day 1 and openly invited the rope. Dave (Executioner on Judy) quietly built a 'vote-steering' case and nominated her. Carol had already confirmed with her Night 1 Oracle guess that Judy was the Jester, but she only voted Innocent and hinted 'a hanged Jester wins' without revealing what she knew. Judy was hanged 10-1. Dave won and left, and the two revenge Divine Attacks killed Erin (Vanilla Villager) and Mallory (Fortune Teller). With Alice (Scout, claimed on Day 1 under pressure) dying to the Katana that same night, the board went from 11 players to 6, with 3 of them Yakuza. From then on the Yakuza had the numbers to block any nomination: half of 6 votes is not a majority. On Day 3 Bob's Lookout correctly caught Grace visiting Alice, and Grace even posted Diviner (a Yakuza-only) results, which outed her, and flatly denied the visit. Heidi and Ivan simply voted No in lockstep, and the Grace nomination stalled at 3 Yes. Grace killed Bob that night. On Day 4 the Yakuza held 3 of 5 votes, so they nominated and hanged Frank. They killed Carol on Night 4 for the win. The Yakuza wasted Night 1 and never used the Clerk or Fabricator tokens, but the Jester hang made all of that irrelevant.

lessons.tip: If your result confirms a Jester or Executioner, reveal it publicly before the nomination vote, or at the latest in your trial speech. Protecting your role is worth far less than stopping a hang that hands Neutrals a win and triggers revenge kills.
lessons.evidence: Carol knew Judy was the Jester after Night 1 but only voted Innocent with a vague 'a hanged Jester wins'. Judy was hanged 10-1. Dave won, and the revenge attacks killed Erin and Mallory, which put the Yakuza at half the table.

lessons.tip: Treat a player who self-nominates and asks for the rope as a probable Jester or Executioner target. Hanging them costs a Village life to revenge, and maybe two if an Executioner rides along. Hang only on a mechanical result. If you must hang, keep the Guilty side a bare majority so fewer Village are in the revenge pool.
lessons.evidence: Judy self-nominated on Day 1 and on trial said 'I'd rather hang on a fair read'. Ten players voted Guilty, and two random Guilty voters (Erin, Mallory) died to the Jester and Executioner revenge attacks.

lessons.tip: Count factions before every vote. Once Evil holds half the living votes, the Village can no longer pass nominations. Once Evil holds a majority, Evil can hang anyone. The Village must avoid losing numbers to wasted hangs before that point. Evil should press its advantage the moment the count allows.
lessons.evidence: On Day 3 (6 alive, 3 Yakuza) Heidi, Ivan and Grace voted No and Bob's nomination of Grace failed at 3 Yes, despite strong evidence. On Day 4 (5 alive) Grace nominated Frank and the Yakuza hanged him 3-2.

lessons.tip: When a Lookout's visit result and a Yakuza-only role claim both point at one player, the players who vote No in lockstep to protect them are the likeliest teammates. Name them publicly and record it in your will so the information outlives you.
lessons.evidence: Heidi and Ivan both voted No on Grace and kept repeating 'need a second source' after Grace had posted Diviner results. That pattern identified the whole Yakuza team, but nobody named the trio together.

lessons.tip: Never post results from a Yakuza-only role, and never flatly deny a visit a Lookout may have seen. Prepare a Village cover claim with a cover action in night chat. Only being at parity saved Grace here.
lessons.evidence: Grace published her Diviner groups on Day 3 and then denied visiting Alice, whom Bob's Lookout had watched. Frank and Carol immediately read her as Yakuza, and Carol's Night 3 Oracle guess confirmed it.

lessons.tip: Open with a mild, friendly private message to your target, then let them make themselves suspicious. Build the case on their own odd plays rather than inventing claims. Nominate when the room is already irritated with them.
lessons.evidence: Dave PM'd Judy on Day 1, absorbed the early heat calmly, then nominated Judy on Day 2 over her unexplained PMs and self-nomination. The nomination passed 10-1 and he won.

lessons.tip: Don't claim an information role on Day 1 just because someone demands results. Claim when you have a result that does work, ideally one that catches someone. An early claim with no payoff just marks you as the Katana target.
lessons.evidence: Alice claimed Scout on Day 1 when Mallory pressed her, posted an uninformative Night 1 result, and was the Yakuza's first kill on Night 2, explicitly 'because she's the live Scout'.

tips_feedback.tip: If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side.
tips_feedback.why: Carol was the only player who acted on it, voting Innocent on Judy. That kept her out of the revenge pool, so she survived to confirm Grace as Yakuza. The ten Guilty voters ignored it and lost Erin and Mallory to revenge.

tips_feedback.why: Players followed the first half: Erin, Grace and Mallory each recited a 'concrete contradiction' about vote-steering. They skipped the Jester caveat, and the ritual gave false confidence for hanging the Jester.

tips_feedback.why: The Village built Judy's hang on her PMs to Bob, a PM-only case with exactly the Jester trail the tip warns about. The Yakuza then turned the 'private whip' framing on Frank's honest PMs to discredit him and hang him.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action... A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof.
tips_feedback.why: Bob, Frank and Carol correctly treated Bob's Night 2 watch (Grace alone visiting Alice, the Katana victim) as near-proof, and Grace was in fact the Katana holder. Parity, not bad reasoning, stopped the hang.

tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza confirmed holder and target in chat every night, and their Katana kills on Alice, Bob and Carol all went through without a missed vote.

issues.description: On Day 3 Grace (Yakuza) publicly posted her Diviner results. Diviner is listed in the public rules as a Yakuza role, so this outed her. Heidi and Ivan then publicly backed those results ('fit the circle'). Carol and Frank immediately pointed out that Diviner is Yakuza-only. This suggests the Yakuza players didn't realize that revealing a Yakuza-only role's results is self-incriminating.

On Day 2 Erin, Frank, Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Judy and Mallory repeatedly demanded Alice's 'Night 2' Scout names, and Judy threatened a Guilty vote if they weren't posted 'next round', although Night 2 had not happened yet. Alice had to say several times that those results would only exist after the coming night. Mallory later cited the impossible demand against Judy while admitting she made it too.

After Night 2 the Scout's passive result ('Tonight Bob, Erin and Heidi were each in a different visit group') was sent to Alice, who had already been told she died that night. Results are being delivered to dead players. It is harmless here, but they should be suppressed or clearly marked.
Frank's last will says he voted Yes on Grace's nomination of him (passed), but the log shows he voted No. The will misstates his own voting record.

On Day 3 Ivan told Bob that 'if your watch is real, it will name whoever visits Alice's group or you next'. This misreads the Lookout: it watches a single living player, not a group, and Alice was already dead.

Several Day 1 players (e.g. Erin) repeated scripted lines such as 'Judy still owes the read Erin asked for', with Erin referring to herself in the third person. The players were copying phrasing almost verbatim rather than tracking who said what.
